title: SDK helpers and control-plane endpoints for permissioned snapshot rollouts with traffic simulation
creator: Riley Chen
description: Build new control-plane endpoints and SDK client helpers to support permission-bound snapshot rollouts. Feature goals: (1) atomic rollout snapshot creation so a rollout can be recreated deterministically from a snapshot; (2) a traffic simulator API to validate traffic-splitting rules against historical and synthetic workloads prior to live promotion; (3) deterministic idempotency and optimistic concurrency for rollout operations to avoid duplicate promotions and ensure safe retries; (4) granular permission checks and audit hooks so platform teams can grant limited rollout actions (create-snapshot, simulate, promote, rollback) to service accounts. This ticket covers API design, server-side reconciliation primitives, SDK-level convenience helpers (JS + Go), integration tests with synthetic traffic, and an initial canary in staging for auto-rollback behaviors.
acceptance_criteria: API endpoints implemented: POST /api/v1/rollouts/snapshots, POST /api/v1/rollouts/:id/simulate, POST /api/v1/rollouts/:id/promote, POST /api/v1/rollouts/:id/rollback
SDK helpers published (npm + go): createSnapshot(), simulateTraffic(), promoteRollout(), rollbackRollout() with built-in idempotency token handling
Server-side snapshotting is deterministic: applying a snapshot to an empty namespace produces the same serving configuration as the original rollout
Traffic simulator can replay historical request distributions and run at least three synthetic scenarios (latency spike, token distribution skew, model-error spike) with pass/fail thresholds
Permission model enforced: role-based checks for create/simulate/promote/rollback with audit log entries written to the event stream
Auto-rollback triggers exercised in staging and meet observability criteria (metric-based triggers + 2-minute cooldown)
test_plan: Unit tests for server snapshot/restore paths (deterministic hashing of config)
Integration: deploy snapshot to isolated cluster and compare endpoints/config hashes
Staging e2e: run simulator against staging tenant with 3 fault scenarios and validate auto-rollback fires
Load test: ensure snapshotting and simulation endpoints handle concurrent jobs from multiple teams without contention
Security test: verify RBAC denies promote to unprivileged service account and audit entries are emitted
rollout_steps: Merge API + SDK change behind feature flag and land server feature toggle
Deploy to staging and run simulator smoke tests with synthetic traffic sets
Open canary to 1% traffic using snapshot-based rollout and monitor for 1 hour
If metrics stable, increase in steps (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%) with automated guards; otherwise, auto-rollback or manual rollback
Post-mortem and update simulator scenarios with any missed failure mode
